title: System Administrator Roadmap
summary: Build Linux and Windows administration skills first, then add networking, security, scripting, virtualization, cloud, automation and infrastructure reliability.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The semester sequence can be shifted to match the university calendar.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Linux/Windows administration, networking, scripting, virtualization, troubleshooting, security fundamentals and internship experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Linux administration, Windows/AD, cloud infrastructure, DevOps/platform engineering or infrastructure security.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Infrastructure automation, reliability, architecture, identity, observability and hybrid-cloud operations.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Platform engineering, cloud architecture, infrastructure strategy, security and technical leadership.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If you choose the four-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for advanced distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, systems security, automation, platform engineering or a substantial infrastructure research/industry project.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Reduce dependence on manual administration by learning infrastructure as code, configuration management, observability, cloud platforms and security automation. The long-term progression is from operating individual servers to owning reliable infrastructure platforms.

items: Infrastructure Architect / Platform Lead / IT Operations Manager (2040–2046)
blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: These are typical stages, not guaranteed promotion dates.
PhD routes

The role can progress from server and endpoint administration toward platform engineering, infrastructure architecture, cloud operations and reliability. Continue developing security, automation, observability and distributed-systems knowledge so that infrastructure decisions can be made at system level rather than through manual administration alone.
